description: JUSTICE is an integrated climate-economy model developed by the HIPPO Lab at TU Delft. It is a simulation and optimisation code designed to test how economic, emissions, damage, abatement and welfare assumptions change distributive justice outcomes. The README describes multiobjective evolutionary and multi-agent reinforcement-learning options. Users define regional socioeconomic and climate assumptions, objective weights and policy choices; outputs are policy pathways and comparisons of welfare or equity under those settings. Geographic aggregation and time horizon follow the configured integrated-assessment experiment. BSD-3-Clause source, citation details and example code are public, while the linked documentation is marked pending in the README. A limitation is that this deliberately simple surrogate of larger models cannot represent detailed engineering networks or stand in for a locally calibrated infrastructure cost-benefit study. It can provide cross-sector policy and equity scenarios that frame infrastructure decisions. The catalogue's data-ipcc-ar6-scenarios-database is a separate source of published pathways. No training, optimisation run or dataset was downloaded.
